title: Ising antiferromagnet on the McLaughlin graph
statement: Put a spin s = +1 or -1 on each of the 275 vertices of the McLaughlin graph, the unique strongly regular graph with parameters (275, 112, 30, 56), whose automorphism group is the sporadic group McL:2 (built here from the Steiner system S(4,7,23) of the binary Golay code: 22 points, 77 heptads through a fixed point, 176 heptads avoiding it). The antiferromagnetic Ising energy is E(s) = sum over the 15,400 edges uv of s_u s_v, so -E counts the edges joining opposite spins minus the others; a ground state is a maximum cut. Every edge lies in 30 triangles, so the model is heavily frustrated. The headline cell: find a configuration with energy below -2968 (ours: 9,184 of the 15,400 edges joining opposite spins). The eigenvalue bound gives E >= -3848.
submission: Text file: 275 spins as + and - (or 1 and -1), in the checker's vertex order (mclaughlin_graph in checkers/orig_phys.py: the points 2..23, then the 77 heptads through 1, then the 176 heptads avoiding 1, heptads sorted).
score: the antiferromagnetic Ising energy E(s), an integer (smaller is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: simulated annealing with single-spin flips, 20,000 sweeps and 30 restarts, then single-flip descent (tools/src/ising.c, mode anneal); runs with other seeds and lengths stop at the same energy

context: The antiferromagnetic Ising model on a graph is the maximum cut problem in physical dress, and on strongly regular graphs it is a clean test of frustration: the Hoffman-type eigenvalue bound E >= m - n(k - theta_min)/2 (m edges, n vertices, degree k, least eigenvalue theta_min) is met exactly by many famous strongly regular graphs (the Gewirtz, Higman-Sims and Gosset graphs, which we checked and set aside, and here the two subconstituents of the McLaughlin graph). The McLaughlin graph (McLaughlin 1969), with spectrum 112, 2^252, (-28)^22, is different. Its bound, a cut of 9,625 edges, is out of reach for parity reasons (an eigenvector of -28 with entries +-1 would sum to zero, impossible for 275 vertices), and our best configurations stop far below it, at 9,184 edges cut, while the 112-vertex graph of the generalised quadrangle GQ(3,9) and the 162-vertex local McLaughlin graph, which are its neighbourhood and non-neighbourhood of a vertex, both reach their bounds. Whether the ground state is the configuration we found, or how far below the bound it lies, is open. The graph has a rank-3 automorphism group of order 1,796,256,000, which a search may exploit.
references: J. McLaughlin, A simple group of order 898,128,000, in: Theory of Finite Groups (Brauer, Sah, eds.), Benjamin, New York, 1969, 109-111
A. E. Brouwer, The McLaughlin graph (22 + 77 + 176 construction from S(4,7,23)), https://aeb.win.tue.nl/graphs/McL.html
B. Mohar, S. Poljak, Eigenvalues and the max-cut problem, Czechoslovak Math. J. 40 (1990) 343-352
S. M. Cioaba, J. H. Koolen, W. Li, Max-cut and extendability of matchings in distance-regular graphs, arXiv:1507.06254

novelty.verdict: new question for this graph: the maximum cut (Ising antiferromagnet) of strongly regular and distance-regular graphs is studied through general bounds, but no value or search for the McLaughlin graph was found, as far as our searches show.
closest: Max-cut of distance-regular graphs (Cioaba, Koolen and Li, arXiv:1507.06254): a general bound of 2/3 of the edges for odd girth 3 here, weaker than the eigenvalue bound, with no values for particular graphs.
Eigenvalue bounds for max-cut (Mohar and Poljak 1990) and our own checks of the Gewirtz, Higman-Sims and Gosset graphs, where the bound is met (listed in dropped.json).
Our Ising problems on the Paley graph of order 101 and on 4-dimensional polytopes: the same model on other graphs.
novelty.benchmark: no spin-glass or max-cut family in the benchmark

rows: its second subconstituent: local McLaughlin graph, srg(162, 56, 10, 24)
first_values.note: Energies from the exact checker (checkers/orig_phys.py builds the graph from the Golay code and checks the parameters); configurations from tools/src/ising.c (simulated annealing, 20,000 sweeps, 20 to 30 restarts); the graph files from tools/mclaughlin_graph.py. The bound for the McLaughlin graph is m - 2 floor(n(k - theta_min)/4 - 1/2) = 15400 - 2 x 9624, the parity argument removing one edge from n(k - theta_min)/4 = 9625.

mclaughlin-second.row: its second subconstituent: local McLaughlin graph, srg(162, 56, 10, 24)

bound.source: the eigenvalue bound: at most n(k - theta_min)/4 = 275 x 140 / 4 = 9625 edges joining opposite spins, with equality only for a +-1 eigenvector of -28, which would sum to zero; with 275 vertices at most 9624, so E >= 15400 - 2 x 9624

baseline.text: -2968 (9,184 of the 15,400 edges joining opposite spins), held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: the configuration in `refs/mclaughlin-ising.txt`.
